title: Slow On the Ramp
hook: The exit is named. The highway is still fast.
scene: Daylight rain, afternoon, I-5 south. The green EXIT ONLY panel already named the leave. You are on the ramp, peeling right off the travel lanes. Their stack on the mainline is still at highway speed. The curve ahead is tight. Dumping speed back there, on the travel lanes, would have turned that stack into a wall of lamps. The ramp is where the number dies. Yuna does not come back on for this.
decision: You have the exit. Where does the speed come off?

options.text: Brake now in the travel lane so you arrive at the ramp already slow
options.result: You dump speed on I-5. The car behind you stands on it. You made a highway stop for a ramp that still had its own pavement.

options.text: Hold highway speed past the gore and brake in the middle of the curve
options.result: You enter the bend still hot. The rear steps out. Yaw on a wet ramp is how a schedule ends, even with a late kit that still delivers.

options.text: Skip this exit and take the next one so you do not have to slow at all
options.result: You miss a named exit because slowing felt rude. Tower 4 just grew a loop. The ramp was the legal place to lose the number.

options.text: Hold speed on the highway, signal early, drop the number on the ramp
options.result: You keep their speed until the ramp owns you. The stalk talked four to six seconds back. On the ramp you tap the brakes and the curve gets the posted number.

debrief: Pick the exit early. Do not slow on the highway. You took the leftover off on the ramp.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part one
source.teaching_target: NEW: PSDP p1 Lesson four – exiting. No DOL Exiting heading — dol n/a. Do not pair 4.12 Signs. Do not steal V-008’s 5.1 conditions cite.
source.stat_cited: PSDP p.31: Identify the exit well ahead of time… don’t slow down on the highway. Start to signal four to six seconds before reaching the ramp.
